html:
Herod the Great was the king of Judea from 37 to 4 BCE, ruling as a client of Rome. He is remembered as a great builder and a cruel ruler.

Named king by the Roman Senate, he kept his throne by loyalty to Mark Antony and then Augustus. He rebuilt the Second Temple in Jerusalem on a vast platform, whose Western Wall still stands. He built the port city of Caesarea, the palace-fortresses of Herodium and Masada, and much more.

He feared plots and had his wife Mariamne and three of his sons killed. The Gospel of Matthew tells that he ordered the massacre of the infants of Bethlehem at the time of the birth of Jesus. After his death his kingdom was split among his sons.
sum: Herod the Great was the king of Judea from 37 to 4 BCE, ruling as a client of Rome. He is remembered as a great builder and a cruel ruler.
